title: Wave 1 — Sung vocals for AI Jam Sessions (vocology, prosody, alignment, SVS routes, eval/HCI)

findings.title: Acoustic Theory of Speech Production
findings.finding: The radiated voice is source × tract filter; independence is only a first approximation.
findings.implication: A formant-shaped oscillator that never generates a glottal flow and then filters it is not a voice.

findings.title: A four-parameter model of glottal flow
findings.finding: The LF source is the derivative of glottal flow (Ee closing discontinuity + Ta return phase), not a harmonic oscillator.
findings.implication: Pitch-shifting a looped aah or Kokoro formant preset without open-quotient/return-phase/Ee cannot produce modal vs breathy vs pressed source spectra.

findings.title: Articulatory interpretation of the singing formant
findings.finding: The singer's formant is a ~2.8 kHz cluster from larynx-tube mismatch, not painted EQ.
findings.implication: SATB additive presets without a narrowed epilarynx will lack male operatic ring.

findings.title: Vocal tract resonances in singing: the soprano voice
findings.finding: When F0 exceeds speech F1, a singer raises R1 to track F0; a fixed tract dumps the remaining harmonic into a dead zone and vowels collapse.
findings.implication: MIDI noteOn that drives F0 above a fixed SATB F1 without jaw/lip modification is the named production error.

findings.title: Nonlinear source-filter coupling in phonation: Theory
findings.finding: At singing pitches source and filter are not independent; F0-F1 crossovers destabilize the folds.
findings.implication: Holding a Pink-Trombone tract fixed while sweeping MIDI through F1 is a documented instability.

findings.title: Bi-stable vocal fold adduction
findings.finding: Registers are glottal shapes, not F0 labels (modal / falsetto / fry).
findings.implication: One LF/waveguide source with only F0 changed cannot be SATB modal vs falsetto.

findings.title: Measurements of the vibrato rate of ten singers
findings.finding: Vibrato is not a 5-7 Hz law; mean 6.0 Hz but rate rises ~15% at endings; single cycles 4.6-8.7 Hz.
findings.implication: A constant LFO on F0 is a cartoon; rate and extent must move with phrase position.

findings.title: Analysis, synthesis, and perception of voice quality variations among female and male talkers
findings.finding: A voice source is mixed periodic + glottal aspiration; aspiration noise cues breathiness more than H1 amplitude.
findings.implication: Additive singing without a glottal noise source cannot do breath, /h/, or phrase-final decay.

findings.title: NHSS: A Speech and Singing Parallel Database
findings.finding: Sung English vowels average 830.5 ms vs 148.0 ms spoken (~5.6×); sung F0 histograms show discrete note peaks speech lacks.
findings.implication: Speech-TTS duration/F0 cannot be copied onto lyrics.

findings.title: XiaoiceSing
findings.finding: Residual log-F0 around MIDI notes won 97.3% A/B vs independent LSTM F0 (RMSE 10.45 vs 13.74 Hz).
findings.implication: F0 is a residual around the score, not a text-predicted contour.

findings.authors: Zhang, Cong, Xue, Xie, Zhu & Bi
findings.title: VISinger
findings.finding: Oracle VITS with speech-style duration is off-key and unintelligible on singing; VISinger uses frame-level prior + phoneme-to-note duration ratio.
findings.implication: Speech-TTS free duration fails because rhythm is score-locked.

findings.title: Sinsy
findings.finding: Time-lag model: consonants start before notated onset; vowel onset tracks the beat; without pitch-norm F0-RMSE jumps ~74 to 264 cents.
findings.implication: Anticipatory coarticulation is a time-lag around the score, not ToBI.

findings.title: NNSVS
findings.finding: Joint DNNs overweight spectrum vs F0; DiffSinger retrain produced discontinuous F0 and unstable vibrato.
findings.implication: Keep F0 as its own residual stream.

findings.title: ExpressiveSinger
findings.finding: High MOS still lacks musicality without explicit performance control of onset deviations, F0 curves, and amplitude envelopes from score+style.
findings.implication: MIDI is the skeleton; performance is predicted around it.

findings.title: TechSinger
findings.finding: L1/FFT F0 cannot capture technique-dependent contours; a pitch predictor conditioned on notes+lyrics+technique beats DiffSinger/VISinger 2 on FFE.
findings.implication: Speech variance-adaptor F0 is the wrong family.

findings.authors: Zheng, Xue, Ren, Ding, Liu & Chen
findings.title: UniVoice
findings.finding: Naïve shared melody conditioning causes gradient conflict (speech PER 12.31%/singing 23.45% vs 5.26%/16.22% with factorization).
findings.implication: Do not reuse speech-TTS prosody as singing melody.

findings.title: When Does a Sung Tone Start?
findings.finding: Sung tone onset is the vowel; accompanists lock piano attacks to vowel onset; consonant-to-beat lag about −100 to +300 ms.
findings.implication: Put the vowel nucleus on the MIDI beat; park onset consonants in the preceding gap.

findings.title: Synchronising speech segments with musical beats in Mandarin and English singing
findings.finding: English vowel beats sit near mid-vowel; sonorant onsets take earlier beats than stops/fricatives.
findings.implication: Fire the English nucleus slightly after note-on.

findings.title: Segment Duration and Proportion in Mandarin Singing
findings.finding: Speech C/V ratios would force 2.5-5 s consonants on a 10 s sung syllable; real singing dumps extra length onto the rime (onset max ~0.28 s).
findings.implication: Freeze onset/coda in a short band; leftover note length goes to the nucleus.

findings.title: NHSS
findings.finding: MFA word-boundary error is 25 ms on speech vs 104 ms on singing.
findings.implication: Do not trust speech MFA boundaries for PhonemeEvents.

findings.title: SongTrans
findings.finding: MFA labels melisma as silence, which then collides with true rests.
findings.implication: Slur/tie flags (or an explicit note-count head) are required.

findings.title: RMSSinger
findings.finding: Fine-grained SVS corpora force MFA then manual phoneme/note edits because one vowel may span multiple notes.
findings.implication: Prefer syllable/word→note maps (slurs for melisma) over phone-level forced alignment.

findings.title: End-to-end Lyrics Alignment
findings.finding: CTC lyrics-to-audio alignment (~0.35 s mean word error) is not lyrics-to-MIDI.
findings.implication: Synthesis from MIDI should stay score-constrained, not unconstrained-aligner-driven.

findings.title: DiffSinger
findings.finding: DiffSinger is score-conditioned SVS (lyrics+pitch+duration → mel); MIDI-B path in official repo; code MIT / OpenVPI Apache 2.0; RTF 0.191.
findings.implication: This family can take MIDI as an acoustic condition; render is offline.

findings.title: NNSVS
findings.finding: NNSVS+WORLD hard-locks phone durations to note length; MIT + modified-BSD; real-time RTF; MOS 3.86 vs recordings 4.39.
findings.implication: Source-filter SVS is the only local real-time score-locked path with permissive licenses.

findings.authors: Zhang, Xue, Li, Xie et al.
findings.title: VISinger 2
findings.finding: Predicted F0 drives a DDSP harmonic oscillator as a hard pitch constraint; official weights not confirmed.
findings.implication: Hybrid DSP+neural SVS can keep F0 hard-constrained.

findings.title: StyleSinger
findings.finding: Notes+lyrics SVS plus reference clip; trained on M4Singer CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; authors will restrict code and models.
findings.implication: Published neural-SVS data/weights are not commercial-safe for a public npm tool.

findings.title: ACE-Step 1.5
findings.finding: Lyrics+caption → mixed song; MIT; BPM/key are metadata, not note MIDI.
findings.implication: Commercially licensed local song generator, not a singing instrument.

findings.title: DiffRhythm 2
findings.finding: Paper states SVS produces vocals with predefined melodies; song generation does not; Apache 2.0 v2 weights.
findings.implication: Cannot honor MIDI; v1 VAE is NC-capped.

findings.title: YuE
findings.finding: Lyrics-to-song; dual-track ICL can change lyrics while preserving accompaniment audio; MIDI is not an input.
findings.implication: Can restyle over an existing mix; cannot sing a supplied MIDI line.

findings.title: so-vits-svc 4.0
findings.finding: Converts a dry vocal into a cloned singer; F0 comes from the source recording, not MIDI; AGPL-3.0.
findings.implication: SVC can retimbre a DSP/MIDI-driven dry vocal; MIDI control stays upstream; AGPL is a ship-blocker for the public package.

findings.title: ITU-R BS.1534-3 MUSHRA
findings.finding: Hidden reference and mid-range anchors are listener-screening tools; exclude listeners who mis-rate them on >15% of items.
findings.implication: Reuse the composition-panel discrimination floor; do not invent a speech-MOS gate.

findings.title: SingMOS-Pro
findings.finding: Lyrics MOS, Melody MOS, and overall are separately rated; UTMOS/DNSMOS correlate poorly with singing.
findings.implication: Admission must score lyrics and pitch-to-score separately.

findings.title: XiaoiceSing
findings.finding: Canonical SVS tests split pronunciation MOS from quality; F0 RMSE 10.45 Hz, Dur RMSE 20.55, F0 CORR 0.99.
findings.implication: A single naturalness MOS hides off-key or unintelligible singing.

findings.title: Sinsy
findings.finding: Without pitch-normalization to the score, F0-RMSE jumps from ~74 to 264 cents.
findings.implication: Score-relative F0 error in cents is the pitch admission metric.

findings.title: VocalRender
findings.finding: Objective RPA/IOU can invert subjective score-following; VocalRender won MS-MOS 2.96 while SoulX-Singer won RPA.
findings.implication: Do not admit a vocal on RPA/MCD alone; CMOS vs a human hidden reference is the perceptual check.

findings.authors: Li, Cui, Manoharan, Dai, Liu & Huang
findings.title: AI singing coach metacognition RCT
findings.finding: LLM singing-coach raised metacognition, not singing scores; the AI was a chatbot plus teacher-demo, not a synthetic singer.
findings.implication: Coaching-layer evidence does not license a model-as-singer.

findings.title: Singing with yourself
findings.finding: Poor-pitch singers match themselves far better than other voices; a perfect other singer is the hard case.
findings.implication: A high-MOS synth of a different identity is a worse pitch-matching model than the learner's own voice.

findings.title: The effect of vocal modeling on pitch-matching accuracy of elementary schoolchildren
findings.finding: Vocal-model identity changes pitch-matching accuracy: child > adult female > adult male.
findings.implication: A synth singer is the wrong tutor if its register/timbre is far from the learner.
